slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 17:19: I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
slides.body: “I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.”
slides.heading: Gen 17:19

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim that Jesus fulfils the promised line through Isaac.
slides.body: God says Sarah will bear Isaac and establishes the covenant with his descendants. Luke later lists Jesus in the line of Jacob, Isaac and Abraham.
slides.heading: Did Isaac's covenant line predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the Christian case for covenant continuity through Isaac to Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis deliberately carries the covenant through Isaac rather than Ishmael. Romans calls Isaac's family the children of promise, and Luke explicitly locates Jesus in that same covenant ancestry.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three distinguishes a genuine genealogy from a specific predictive prophecy.
slides.body: Genesis predicts Isaac, then many descendants—not one named Messiah. Romans discusses who counts as God's promised people; it never calls Jesus the fulfilment of this verse. Luke establishes ancestry, but many descendants share it.
slides.heading: Ancestry is not unique identification

title: Did Isaac's covenant line predict Jesus?
